title: Comparing rational numbers
competency: Compare rational numbers using decimals, common denominators, cross-products and the number line.

keywords.def: A number written with a decimal point, like 4.25.
The value of a digit from its position: ones, tenths, hundredths, …
Fractions that mark the same point on the number line, like 1/2 and 2/4.
Least common multiple: the smallest number that two numbers both divide.
To compare a/b and c/d, compare a × d with b × c.
A line with 0 in the middle. The number further left is smaller.

en.text: To compare decimals, start from the left. Compare the integer parts. If they are equal, compare tenths, then hundredths. The first place that differs decides.

am.text: አስርዮሾችን ለማነፃፀር ከግራ ጀምር። መጀመሪያ ሙሉ ክፍሎቹን አነፃፅር። እኩል ከሆኑ አስረኛዎችን፣ ከዚያ መቶኛዎችን አነፃፅር።

screens.title: Cold night
screens.ask: One night Debre Birhan was −2 °C and Addis Ababa was 8 °C. Which was colder?
screens.after:
On the number line, −2 is left of 0 and 8 is right of 0.
The number further left is smaller: −2 < 8.
A smaller temperature is colder.
So Debre Birhan was colder.

screens.title: Comparing decimals
paras: Think of wins and losses, temperatures, profit and loss.
A rational number a/b becomes a decimal when you divide a by b.
screens.note: Compare decimals place by place from the left: integer part, then tenths, then hundredths.

screens.title: Example: 6.7 and 6.89 on the line

points.info: 8 tenths and 9 hundredths past 6. It is further right, so it is bigger.

screens.ask: Tap both points. Which one is further right?

screens.title: Key words
defs: A number written with a decimal point, like 4.25.
The value of a digit from its position: ones, tenths, hundredths, …

screens.text: Compare the decimals: which sign is correct? 6.7 ? 6.89
screens.why:
Write both with two decimal places: 6.70 and 6.89.
Integer parts: 6 = 6, equal.
Tenths: 7 < 8.
So 6.7 < 6.89. (6.89 has more digits, but that is not why it is bigger.)

screens.text: Compare negative integers: which sign is correct? −3 ? −5
screens.why:
On the number line, −3 is 3 units left of 0 and −5 is 5 units left of 0.
−5 is further left, so −5 is smaller.
So −3 > −5.
(5 > 3, but for negatives the bigger size is the smaller number.)

screens.text: Compare the decimals: true or false? 6.53 < 6.053
screens.why:
Write both with three decimal places: 6.530 and 6.053.
Integer parts: 6 = 6.
Tenths: 5 > 0.
So 6.53 > 6.053, and the statement is false.

screens.text: Compare decimals: which number is the largest?
screens.why:
Write all with three decimal places: 0.405, 0.450, 0.400, 0.045.
Tenths: 4, 4, 4 and 0. So 0.045 is the smallest.
Hundredths of the others: 0, 5 and 0.
0.450 has the most hundredths, so 0.45 is the largest.
screens.clue: Write them all with three decimal places: 0.405, 0.450, 0.400, 0.045.

en.text: With the same denominator, the bigger numerator is bigger. With different denominators, change both to the LCM of the denominators and compare numerators. Or cross-multiply: a/b > c/d when a × d > b × c.

am.text: ተመሳሳይ ተካፋይ ሲኖር ትልቅ ላዕላይ ያለው ይበልጣል። የተለያየ ከሆነ ወደ ትንሹ የጋራ ብዜት ቀይርና ላዕላዮቹን አነፃፅር። ወይም መስቀለኛ አባዛ።

screens.title: Which is bigger, 3/5 or 1/2?
screens.after:
Both bars are the same whole.
The blue part (3/5) is a little longer than the orange part (1/2).
So 3/5 > 1/2. Below you will prove it with numbers.

screens.title: Same denominator
paras: Same denominators: the bigger numerator is the bigger number.

screens.title: Different denominators
paras: Equivalent fractions mark the same point on the number line.
Method 1: find the LCM of the denominators. Rewrite both fractions. Compare the numerators.
Method 2 (cross-product): a/b < c/d when a × d < b × c.
screens.note: a/b = (a × m)/(b × m) for any non-zero integer m.

screens.title: Equivalent fractions: 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8
screens.after:
All three shaded parts are the same length.
1/2 = (1 × 2)/(2 × 2) = 2/4 and 1/2 = (1 × 4)/(2 × 4) = 4/8.
Equivalent fractions mark the same point on the number line.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Fractions that mark the same point on the number line, like 1/2 and 2/4.
The smallest number that two numbers both divide.
To compare a/b and c/d, compare a × d with b × c.

screens.title: 3/5 and 1/2
steps: The denominators are 5 and 2. Their LCM is 10.
10 ÷ 5 = 2, so multiply top and bottom of 3/5 by 2: (3 × 2)/(5 × 2) = 6/10.
10 ÷ 2 = 5, so multiply top and bottom of 1/2 by 5: (1 × 5)/(2 × 5) = 5/10.
Now the denominators are equal. Compare the numerators: 6 > 5.

screens.text: Compare fractions with different denominators: which sign is correct? 11/16 ? 7/8
Compare fractions by cross-multiplying: which sign is correct? 5/7 ? 8/3
screens.why:
Cross-multiply: 5 × 3 = 15 (left) and 7 × 8 = 56 (right).
15 < 56.
So 5/7 < 8/3.
Check: 5/7 is less than 1, and 8/3 = 2 2/3 is more than 1.

screens.text: Compare a negative and a positive fraction: which sign is correct? −12/7 ? 6/9
screens.why:
−12/7 is negative: it is left of 0.
6/9 is positive: it is right of 0.
Every negative number is less than every positive number.
So −12/7 < 6/9.

screens.ask: Equivalent fractions: fill in the numerator. 3/5 = ___/10
screens.why:
5 × 2 = 10, so the bottom was multiplied by 2.
Multiply the top by the same number: 3 × 2 = 6.
So 3/5 = 6/10.
Check: 6/10 = 0.6 and 3/5 = 0.6.

Cross-multiply: 12 × 15 = 180 and 8 × 10 = 80.
180 ≠ 80, so they are not equal.
Also: 12/8 = 1 1/2 is more than 1, and 10/15 = 2/3 is less than 1.
False.

screens.text: Compare negative fractions: which sign is correct? −5/6 ? −7/9
screens.why:
First compare the sizes 5/6 and 7/9. The LCM of 6 and 9 is 18.
5/6 = (5 × 3)/(6 × 3) = 15/18 and 7/9 = (7 × 2)/(9 × 2) = 14/18.
15/18 > 14/18, so 5/6 has the bigger size.
For negatives, the bigger size is further left: −5/6 < −7/9.
screens.clue: Compare the sizes first. With negatives, bigger size means smaller number.

en.text: On a number line the number further left is smaller. Every positive number is greater than every negative number. Of two negatives, the one with the bigger absolute value is smaller.

am.text: በቁጥር መስመር ላይ በግራ ያለው ያንሳል። ማንኛውም አዎንታዊ ቁጥር ከማንኛውም አሉታዊ ቁጥር ይበልጣል። ከሁለት አሉታዊዎች ፍጹም ዋጋው የሚበልጠው ያንሳል።

points.info: is the smallest here: furthest left.
is less than 0 and greater than −1.
sits between the negatives and positives.

screens.ask: Tap the points from left to right. Which one is smallest?

screens.title: Comparing with the number line
paras: Of two numbers on the line, the one on the left is smaller.
Tap each fact below to see an example.

screens.title: Four facts from the number line
items: Every positive number is right of 0, so it is greater than 0. Example: 1/2 > 0.
Every negative number is left of 0, so it is less than 0. Example: −1/2 < 0.
Positives are right of every negative. Example: 1/2 > −1.
The bigger absolute value is further left, so it is smaller. Example: −45 < −23.

screens.title: Left is smaller
defs: A line with 0 in the middle. The number further left is smaller.

screens.text: Compare negative numbers: which is smaller, −45 or −23?
screens.why:
|−45| = 45 and |−23| = 23.
−45 is further from 0 on the left side.
The number further left is smaller.
So −45 is smaller: −45 < −23.

screens.text: Compare on the number line: which is further to the left?
screens.why:
Write both as decimals: −1/3 ≈ −0.33 and −1.5.
In size, 1.5 > 0.33.
For negatives, the bigger size is further left.
So −1.5 is further left.

screens.text: Absolute value and comparing: true or false? |−3/5| < 3/5
screens.why:
Find the absolute value first: |−3/5| = 3/5.
So the statement says 3/5 < 3/5.
A number is not less than itself; they are equal.
False.

screens.text: Compare on the number line: a is a negative number and b is a positive number. Which is ALWAYS true?
screens.why:
Every negative number is left of 0.
Every positive number is right of 0.
So a is always left of b: a < b.
|a| < |b| is not always true: try a = −10 and b = 1, then |a| = 10 > 1.
screens.clue: Think of the number line. Try some numbers.

items.text: Compare a negative and a positive decimal: true or false? −0.15 < 1.5
items.why:
−0.15 is negative, so it is left of 0.
1.5 is positive, so it is right of 0.
A negative is always less than a positive.
True.

items.text: Compare fractions with the same denominator: true or false? 23/5 > 32/5
items.why:
The denominators are the same (5).
So compare the numerators: 23 and 32.
23 < 32, so 23/5 < 32/5.
The statement is false.

items.text: Compare a mixed number and a fraction: true or false? 3 5/7 > 21/6
Mixed and improper fractions: true or false? 3 4/7 = 25/7
items.why:
Change 3 4/7 to an improper fraction.
3 wholes = 3 × 7 = 21 sevenths.
21 + 4 = 25 sevenths, so 3 4/7 = 25/7.
True.
items.clue: Change the mixed number to an improper fraction.

items.text: Compare negative fractions: which sign is correct? −21/12 ? −28/16
items.why:
Simplify −21/12: divide top and bottom by 3: −7/4.
Simplify −28/16: divide top and bottom by 4: −7/4.
Both equal −7/4.
So −21/12 = −28/16.

items.text: Compare a fraction and a decimal: which sign is correct? 8/20 ? 0.35
items.why:
Change 8/20 to a decimal: 8/20 = 4/10 = 0.4.
Compare 0.40 and 0.35.
Tenths: 4 > 3.
So 8/20 > 0.35.

test.text: Compare fractions: which sign is correct? 3/4 ? 5/7
Compare the decimals: which sign is correct? 4.07 ? 4.7
test.why:
Write 4.7 as 4.70.
Integer parts: 4 = 4.
Tenths: 0 < 7.
So 4.07 < 4.7.

test.text: Compare negative fractions: which sign is correct? −2/3 ? −3/4
test.why:
Compare the sizes: 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12.
2/3 is the smaller size.
For negatives, the smaller size is closer to 0, so it is bigger.
So −2/3 > −3/4.

test.text: Compare negative fractions: true or false? −3/4 < −2/3
test.why:
LCM of 4 and 3 is 12: 3/4 = 9/12 and 2/3 = 8/12.
3/4 has the bigger size.
For negatives, the bigger size is further left.
So −3/4 < −2/3: true.

test.text: Compare negative numbers: which is the largest?
test.why:
Change all to decimals: −0.3, −1/4 = −0.25, −0.35, −2/5 = −0.4.
All are negative, so the largest is the one closest to 0.
The smallest size is 0.25.
So −1/4 is the largest.

notes.text: The book's equivalent-fractions note says m is a rational number different from 0; m must be a non-zero integer for a/b = (a × m)/(b × m) to stay a fraction of integers. Shown as an integer here.

screens.text: List multiples until one appears in both lists.
steps: 12 is the first one in both lists.

screens.text: What is the LCM of 6 and 8?
screens.why: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24. 24 is also a multiple of 6.
screens.clue: List multiples of 8 and stop at the first that 6 divides.
